title: 1982 FIFA World Cup
prose:
From 13 June to 11 July 1982, Spain hosted the twelfth FIFA World Cup, the first contested by 24 teams after expansion from 16, a widening that opened more places for the African and Asian confederations. The enlarged field made it the largest World Cup to that point, with a total attendance of 2,109,723 across 52 matches, an average of about 40,572 per game. The format paired a first round of six groups of four, from which the top two advanced, with an unusual second group stage of four groups of three; the four group winners reached the semi-finals, followed by a knockout final and third-place match.

The road to the title belonged to Italy, who advanced from the first group stage without a single win, drawing all three matches and progressing on goals scored. The turning point came in the second stage, where the previously goalless Paolo Rossi struck a hat-trick to knock out the favourites Brazil. Rossi went on to top the scoring charts with six goals, won the inaugural Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, and uniquely claimed the World Cup, the top-scorer title and the Golden Ball at the same edition. At 40, Italy captain and goalkeeper Dino Zoff became the oldest player to win the World Cup.

In the final at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, Italy defeated West Germany 3-1 in full time, with no extra time needed. Rossi opened the scoring in the 57th minute, Marco Tardelli added a second in the 69th and Alessandro Altobelli a third in the 81st, before Paul Breitner pulled one back for West Germany in the 83rd. It was Italy's third world title; West Germany finished runners-up and Poland took third.

The tournament produced enduring storylines. West Germany's semi-final against France finished 3-3 after extra time and was decided by the first penalty shootout in World Cup history, won 5-4; the match is also remembered for Harald Schumacher's violent collision with Patrick Battiston, for which no foul was given. The 'Disgrace of Gijon', West Germany's 1-0 win over Austria that eliminated Algeria, later prompted FIFA to schedule final group matches simultaneously. Hungary's 10-1 defeat of El Salvador remains the largest winning margin in World Cup finals history.
